interactions.summary: Jiang extends the will model by arguing that heaven only grants what one intensely wants, and he glosses Piccarda's remaining in the lowest sphere as refusal to want anything beyond it.
A student sharpens Jiang's point by defining free will as the power to will what one wants, not merely to act, and another student asks whether this resembles Nietzsche's will to power.

Jiang accepts comparisons to Nietzsche and self-efficacy, then translates the whole model into popular 'manifestation' language and says the deeper issue is not good versus evil but the form taken by will.

claims.claim: Jiang says the universe grants whatever a person truly wants, so Piccarda's remaining in the lower sphere reveals that she does not genuinely want to move beyond it.
Jiang frames Dante's world as a constant communication between person and universe in which focused intentionality determines what can be achieved.
A student defines free will here as the ability to will what one wants rather than merely the ability to perform chosen actions, and Jiang explicitly endorses that formulation.
claims.temporal_scope: Student formulation ratified by Jiang on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Jiang says Dante's theory of will is very similar to Nietzsche's and also comparable to psychological self-efficacy, because all three stress belief or willing as the precondition of accomplishment.
Jiang translates the model into the popular term 'manifestation' and then radicalizes it by saying the universe contains no good and evil, only will and the choices made with it.

signature_moments.moment: Free will gets redefined as the capacity to will your desire, not just to execute an action.
signature_moments.source_phrase: being able to will what you want
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the packet its cleanest philosophical compression of Jiang's account of agency.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says manifestation, Nietzsche, and Dante all converge on a universe where will outruns morality.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there's really no good and evil in the universe there's just will
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's most provocative statement and the one most likely to shape the public read or later lens pressure.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: In this discussion, the power not just to act but to shape the very wanting that precedes action.
The psychology concept a student uses to compare Jiang's will model to belief in one's own capacity to accomplish a task.
Jiang's popular-language label for willing an imagined reality into being.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet broadens the Piccarda discussion into a general theory of will by linking Dante to manifestation language, Nietzsche, and self-efficacy.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student says 'Bandora,' but the stable point is a comparison to self-efficacy rather than exact scholarly naming.
